title: GPU resilience scenario sprint readout - 2027-05-04
content:
Weekly infra sync: GPU Resilience Scenario — sprint readout (2027-05-04)

Attendees: Aisha Chen (owner), Ravi Kapoor, Elena Park, Jonas Müller, Samira Ortiz (SRE), Marco Li (release eng) — plus on-call rotation (listed in linked artifacts).

Purpose: capture findings from the 3-day surge/resilience scenario we ran across US-W, EU-W, AP-S. Main focus: priming behavior, soft-eviction effects, regional failover latency, and cost delta for maintaining spare pools. Not a final runbook; draft for review by infra and SRE.

TL;DR:
- Priming live workloads before traffic surges materially reduces tail latency and request failures during warm-up windows.
- Maintaining a modest reserved pool per region (20-40 GPUs depending on model class) yields best tradeoff for 95th latency vs cost.
- Soft-eviction prototype worked but needs improved scoring (age + last-used + model-hotness) to avoid noisy evictions.
- GCP quota bottle-necks in AP-S were the primary blocker for automated regional failover in one test. Procurement ticket created.

Observations / metrics (aggregate across runs):
- Baseline (no priming): 95p latency for text-gen 8k context w/ LlamaX-70B ~ 210ms token gen. Initial 2-minute surge spikes added 30–60% extra latency and 2.7% request failures due to container spin-up/prewarmed cache misses.
- With priming (prefix prefill + KV cache seeding): 95p dropped to ~145ms, peak failures <0.5%. Cold-start window reduced from ~120s to ~22s for routed requests.
- Soft-eviction prototype: average eviction churn reduced by 18% vs immediate LRU under high churn. However, 3/12 eviction events accidentally targeted pinned RDMA lanes — root cause: metric namespace mismatch.
- Cost impact: keeping a regional spare pool sized at 25 GPUs (A100-80GB equiv) increased steady-state spend by ~6.8% but reduced simulated SLA penalties in stress tests by ~41%.
- Inter-region failover: cross-region routing added ~80–150ms RTT; combined with cold-starts this produced user-visible latency >500ms in one EU->US failover test. Priming reduced that to ~210–260ms — acceptable for lower-tier routes but not for latency-sensitive customers.

Regional notes: 
- us-west-2: cleanest results. Autoscaler hooks handled surge bursts reliably once priming was engaged. Recommended spare pool: 30 GPUs for current qps (see capacity calc below).
- eu-west-1: slightly higher preemption risk from cloud provider (spot reclaim tests). Soft-eviction needs to avoid evicting pinned enterprise workloads. Recommend adding 'pinned' tag on enterprise pods and exclude from eviction policy.
- ap-southeast-1: constrained by GCP per-project GPU quota. During simulated failover, quota exhaustion prevented full warm-up. Procurement/Quota ticket (GPO-789) opened; ETA for quota bump optimistic: 2–3 weeks. Temporary mitigation: enable regional routing to nearest lower-cost partner edge (see GPO-789 notes).

Capacity quick calc (notes, not definitive):
- Current sustained token throughput (global): ~680k tokens/s peak.
- Typical LlamaX-70B throughput per A100 equiv ~22k tokens/s at tuned batching profiles.
- Spare pool sizing: region_spare = ceil((expected_peak_routing_fraction * peak_tokens) / per_gpu_capacity) * safety_margin
  Example us-west: peak_tokens_local=180k tokens/s -> 180k/22k≈8.2 -> with safety_margin 3.5x -> ~29 GPUs -> choose 30.

Decisions made in meeting: 
1) Approve pilot of regional spare pools for 4 regions (US-W, EU-W, AP-SE, US-E) for next sprint. Pilot config: us-west-2=30, eu-west-1=24, ap-southeast-1=16, us-east-1=20.
2) Merge soft-eviction scoring improvements (age + last-used + model-hotness) into staging branch; keep eviction safe-list for enterprise tags. Owner: Ravi Kapoor.
3) Priming: adopt prefix prefill + KV seed for all model routes with >1% latency sensitivity. Implementation tracked in INFRA-2134.
4) Failover behavior: default for latency-sensitive routes = avoid cross-region fallback unless spare capacity within region <10% of pool.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ravi Kapoor — implement eviction scoring changes + add enterprise safe-list (INFRA-2134). Due 2027-05-11.
- Elena Park — finalize cost model for regional spare pools and run cost/perf sensitivity matrix with finance. Due 2027-05-08.
- Jonas Müller — prep AP-S contingency plan for quota delays (work with procurement on GPO-789). Due 2027-05-10.
- Samira Ortiz (SRE) — add observability dashboards for priming effectiveness (kv-hit, time-to-first-token post-failover). Due 2027-05-09.
- Marco Li — smoke test canary funnel for enterprise-pinned pods to ensure eviction safety. Due 2027-05-12.

Open questions / risks: 
- How to price spare-pool cost back to customers? (finance & product input needed)
- Are we comfortable with the added steady-state spend for smaller customers on hosted tier? (product gating)
- Risk: if cloud providers change reclamation semantics, our soft-eviction heuristics may not hold — need a re-run as part of quarterly priming exercise.

Notes / workbench (raw):
- Experiment IDs: surge-run-2027-05-02-a..d (linked in INFRA-2134). 
- Quick commands used:
  * priming-run: ./tools/priming/run.sh --region us-west-2 --model LlamaX-70B --pool 30 --prefix-seed 12k
  * eviction-sim: python infra/sim/evict_sim.py --policy soft-score --trace samples/surge-2027-04-29.json
- Observability notes: need to add a KV-cache hit metric at the router hop; currently only instrumented at runtime server (gap causing confusion in the priming dashboard).

Next steps / cadence:
- Short-term (this sprint): implement scoring changes, create priming dashboards, spin pilot spare pools in staging, run one controlled failover per region by 2027-05-14.
- Medium-term (next 6 weeks): evaluate cost impact, update routing policy defaults, create customer-facing KB for enterprise customers about pinned capacity options.
- Longer-term: bake priming into autoscaler lifecycle; consider a hybrid billing model for reserved warm pools.

References / links: Confluence readout (confluence:CONF-589), infra PR for soft-eviction (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423), tickets INFRA-2134, GPO-789, slack thread #gpu-ops/thread-16234.

Notes to self: this doc is a working readout; expect edits as owners update tickets. Add raw logs and the csv from surge-run outputs to the 'misc' folder if needed for postmortem.
